title: Mineral nutrition
group: BIO-EVOL / BIO-ECOL / BIO-PLANT — Evolution, Ecology & Plants
examples: What are the main groups of essential plant nutrients?
How do plants absorb minerals from the soil?
What causes yellowing leaves in plants?

explain.say: Some minerals are vital for plant life to thrive.
The primary macronutrients are nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium.

draw.text: N, P, K are major nutrients

explain.say: Magnesium is important for the structure of the chlorophyll molecule.
Iron is a micronutrient needed for the synthesis of chlorophyll.
Nitrogen deficiency often shows as general yellowing of older leaves.
A common mistake is thinking all yellowing means nitrogen deficiency.

faq.q: What is the difference between a macronutrient and a micronutrient?
faq.a: Macronutrients are minerals plants need in relatively large amounts for growth. Micronutrients are minerals plants need but only in very small amounts.
asks: Are all nutrients needed in large amounts?

faq.q: Why does nitrogen deficiency affect older leaves first?
faq.a: Plants can move mobile nutrients like nitrogen from older leaves to support new growth. This process leaves the older parts deficient.

faq.q: What is the specific symptom of iron deficiency?
faq.a: Iron deficiency often causes new leaves to become pale green or yellow, while the veins remain distinct and green.
asks: How do I spot iron problems?
Is it always the new leaves affected?

faq.q: Do all deficiency symptoms look the same?
faq.a: No, the pattern of yellowing or spotting is often unique to the specific missing mineral element. Observing the pattern is key.
asks: Can I tell which nutrient is missing?
Is there a pattern to the symptoms?

faq.q: What are the essential elements for plant life?
faq.a: The essential elements include macronutrients like Nitrogen, Phosphorus, and Potassium, and micronutrients like Iron and Magnesium.
asks: What minerals do plants absolutely need?

faq.q: How do I know if a plant needs more nitrogen?
faq.a: If the older leaves are turning uniformly yellow, it suggests the plant is mobilizing nitrogen from those older parts.
asks: If the old leaves yellow, what is it?

facts: Nitrogen is crucial for forming amino acids and proteins in plants.
Phosphorus is vital for energy transfer molecules like ATP.
Magnesium is the central atom in the chlorophyll molecule.
Iron deficiency often presents as interveinal chlorosis on new growth.

quiz.say: A plant shows yellowing on its oldest leaves first. Which nutrient is likely deficient?
quiz.show: Oldest leaves yellowing: N or Fe?
quiz.why: Nitrogen is a mobile nutrient, so the plant moves it from older leaves to support new growth.

wrong.0: Phosphorus deficiency usually causes dark green or purplish discoloration, not general yellowing of old leaves.
wrong.1: Iron deficiency typically affects the newest growth first, causing yellowing between the veins.
wrong.2: Potassium deficiency often causes yellowing or browning around the edges of older leaves, but N is a more classic answer for general old leaf yellowing.

quiz.say: If the newest leaves are yellow, but the veins remain green, what is the likely problem?
quiz.show: New leaves yellow, veins green: Mg or Fe?
quiz.why: Iron is often poorly utilized by the plant, leading to chlorosis (yellowing) in new growth where it is needed most.

wrong.0: Nitrogen deficiency affects older leaves first because it is mobile.
wrong.1: Potassium deficiency symptoms are usually related to leaf margins burning or yellowing.
wrong.3: Magnesium deficiency usually shows yellowing between the veins on older leaves, not just the newest ones.

quiz.say: Which nutrient is essential for the structure of the chlorophyll molecule?
quiz.why: Magnesium ions form the central core atom within the chlorophyll pigment molecule.

wrong.0: Iron is important for electron transport in photosynthesis, but magnesium is the central atom in the chlorophyll structure.
wrong.1: Nitrogen is needed to build the protein parts of the photosynthetic machinery, but it is not the central atom of the pigment itself.
wrong.2: Phosphorus is critical for energy transfer (ATP) but is not a structural component of the chlorophyll molecule.
